finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any authenticated user, including one with no permissions, can run the destructive purgeAll() operation. The sibling handler rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure.
finding.source: Any authenticated low-privilege user sends a request to the purge endpoint. The user's Perms map lacks "admin".
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a protected admin operation that purges data.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller's User from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for a non-admin, but the return value is ignored and there is no early return
The handler writes "purged" with a 200 status

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm only returns a bool and does not write a response or abort. No other check exists in the handler. Middleware is not present in this directory, so it could not be verified. Even if middleware exists, this handler's own admin check is a no-op. By contrast, rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 uses mustPerm and returns on failure. A nil-map lookup returns false, so no implicit denial happens elsewhere.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12 returns a bool only; its result is discarded at handlers.go:26; no router/middleware is present in the directory)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement, so its bool result is ignored and purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm and returns at handlers.go:33-35.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none effective: checkPerm (handlers.go:12) returns a bool and is called as a bare statement at line 26; mustPerm is only used in rotateKeys
verdict_facts.reason: handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's bool with no early return, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 which returns on mustPerm failure.
